gaps.sentence: She took notes during the seminar ___ she could write it up that evening.
gaps.explanation: 'So that' introduces the purpose of the action.

gaps.sentence: She took a map ___ she wouldn't get lost.
___ I thoroughly enjoyed the novel, the sequel left me cold.
gaps.explanation: Concessive 'while' = although, introducing the clause of concession.

gaps.sentence: In Sweden the shops close early, ___ in Spain they stay open until ten.
gaps.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts parallel facts about two countries.

gaps.sentence: The treatment doesn't weaken patients; ___, it speeds up their recovery.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' asserts the opposite of what was just said.

gaps.sentence: ___ the theory is elegant, the data simply don't support it.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' grants the fact (the theory is elegant) before contradicting it.

gaps.sentence: ___ she was utterly exhausted, she stayed to help clear up.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' concedes a known fact: she was exhausted and still stayed.

gaps.sentence: She is not only a gifted violinist ___ a composer of some note.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only A but also B' joins the two parallel noun phrases.
